'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[Taliban]] [[insurgent]]s enter [[Qala e Naw]], the [[provinces of Afghanistan|provincial]] capital of [[Badghis Province]], with heavy fighting reported as the [[militant]]s move "towards the centre of the city". All [[government of Afghanistan|government]] officials in the city have been moved to a nearby [[Afghan National Army|army base]], while the Taliban have freed about 400 prisoners from the city's prison. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-57748695 (BBC News)]
*The [[United States Armed Forces]] report that two personnel were injured in rocket attacks on [[Al Asad Airbase]] in [[Iraq]], which houses US troops. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/7/barrage-of-rockets-fired-at-airbase-housing-us-troops-in-iraq (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Assassination of Jovenel Moïse]]
**[[President of Haiti|Haitian President]] [[Jovenel Moïse]] is [[Assassination|assassinated]] by a squad of gunmen at his home in [[Pétion-Ville]]. His wife, [[First Ladies and Gentlemen of Haiti|First Lady]] [[Martine Moïse]], is also shot and critically wounded. [https://apnews.com/article/caribbean-haiti-government-and-politics-b56a0f8fec0832028bdc51e8d59c6af2 (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a record 201 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 15,593. [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2021/07/07/bangladesh-again-shatters-single-day-death-record-with-201-fatalities (''Dhaka Tribune'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record for the third consecutive day of 34,379 new cases and a record for the fourth consecutive day of 1,040 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2.37 million and the nationwide death toll to 62,908. [https://nasional.kompas.com/read/2021/07/07/16152471/bertambah-34379-kasus-covid-19-dalam-sehari-rekor-tertinggi-selama-pandemi (Kompas.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]]n [[Government of Sri Lanka|authorities]] ban all public gatherings and protests under the instruction of the Director General of Health Services due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.aninews.in/news/world/asia/sri-lanka-bans-all-public-gatherings-as-covid-19-cases-soar20210707230553/ (ANI News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
***[[Fiji]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 791 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the national total of cases to 7,940. The [[Ministry of Health and Medical Services (Fiji)|Ministry of Health and Medical Services]] also reports three deaths from COVID-19, all in [[Suva]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/446412/fiji-announces-record-number-of-new-covid-19-cases-three-deaths (RNZ)]
***The Fiji police warns citizens that those caught not wearing a face mask when outdoors or in lockdown or containment areas will be arrested under possible penalties of five years' imprisonment, a fine of up to [[Fijian dollar|FJ$]]10,000 or both, as the country faces a wave of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.fbcnews.com.fj/news/covid-19/not-wearing-mask-can-lead-to-imprisonment/ (FBC)] 
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]]
***[[Tunisia]] reports a record 9,823 new cases and 134 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the national total of confirmed cases to 464,914 and the nationwide death toll to 15,735. [https://news-tunisia.tunisienumerique.com/tunisia-record-breaking-9823-cases-of-covid-19-and-134-deaths-in-24-hours/ (Tunisie Numérique)] 
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
***The [[United Kingdom]] reports 32,548 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of new cases since January 22. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/health/covid-uk-daily-cases-latest-b1879855.html (''The Independent'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Centerra Gold]] files additional claims against the [[Politics of Kyrgyzstan|Kyrgyz government]] in binding arbitration and asserted claims against state-owned Kyrgyzaltyn JSC in response to the seizure of the [[Kumtor Gold Mine]] in [[Kyrgyzstan]]. [https://lethbridgeherald.com/business/2021/07/07/centerra-gold-files-additional-claims-in-arbitration-relating-to-seized-asian-mine/ (''Lethbridge Herald'')]
*The [[Assembly of the Republic of Kosovo]] votes 89–0 to pass a resolution officially condemning the [[Srebrenica massacre]] and establishing a commemorative holiday for its victims. [[Kosovo Serbs|Serb minority]]-interests party [[Serb List (Kosovo)|Serb List]] boycotted the vote. [https://www.rferl.org/a/kosovo-parliament-srebrenica-condemnation/31345931.html (RFEL)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Political impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Prime Minister of India|Indian Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] dismisses 12 cabinet ministers, including [[Ministry of Health and Family Welfare|Health Minister]] [[Harsh Vardhan (Delhi politician)|Harsh Vardhan]], following intense criticisms over his handling of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in India|COVID-19 pandemic]]. [[Ravi Shankar Prasad]], who held multiple concurrent positions as [[Ministry of Law and Justice (India)|Law]], [[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology|Information Technology]], and [[Ministry of Communications (India)|Communications Minister]], also resigns. [https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/south-asia/article/3140229/indias-modi-reshuffles-cabinet-amid-drop-popularity-during (''South China Morning Post'')]
**[[2020–21 Malaysian political crisis]]
***The [[United Malays National Organisation]] (UMNO), the largest party in the ruling [[Perikatan Nasional]] coalition, withdraws its support for [[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Malaysian Prime Minister]] [[Muhyiddin Yassin]] and calls for his resignation. The move occurred despite Yassin appointing UMNO vice-president [[Ismail Sabri Yaakob]] as [[Deputy Prime Minister of Malaysia|Deputy Prime Minister]] and major party stalwart [[Hishammuddin Hussein]] as [[Senior Minister of Malaysia|Senior Security Minister]] earlier in the day in order to prevent this. UMNO president [[Ahmad Zahid Hamidi]] says that the decision was due to Yassin's poor handling of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia|COVID-19 pandemic]], with Hamidi specifically singling out the ineffective and contradictory implementation of the [[Malaysian movement control order|lockdowns]] as the main point of contention. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/umno-withdraws-support-for-malaysias-pm-muhyiddin-calls-for-his-resignation (''The Straits Times'')] [https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/politics/article/3140197/malaysias-prime-minister-muhyiddin-appoints-umno-stalwart-ismail (''South China Morning Post'')]
*[[2021 Swedish government crisis]]
**[[Prime Minister of Sweden]] [[Stefan Löfven]] is narrowly re-elected to stay in power after losing a [[no confidence vote]] last month. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/07/06/stefan-lofven-swedish-caretaker-pm-faces-parliament-vote-to-form-new-government (Euronews)]
*[[2021 Israeli presidential election]]
**[[Isaac Herzog]] is sworn in as the [[President of Israel]] in a ceremony at the [[Knesset]], where he takes the oath of office using the same 107-year-old Bible that his father [[Chaim Herzog]] used when he assumed the presidency in 1983. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/herzog-to-take-office-as-israels-11th-president-in-a-day-of-pomp-and-ceremony/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[Ursula von der Leyen]], the [[President of the European Commission]], warns [[Hungary]] to repeal its [[Hungarian anti-LGBT law|controversial amendments to its Child Protection Act]], which bans the dissemination of content in schools deemed to "promote homosexuality", or else face "the full force of EU law". Poland is expected to block any attempt to impose the maximum EU penalty of suspending Hungary's voting rights. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/a-disgrace-hungary-must-ditch-anti-lgbt-law-eu-executive-says-2021-07-07/ (Reuters)] [https://www.euronews.com/2021/07/07/us-hungary-lgbt-law (Euronews)]

'''Sports'''
*[[UEFA Euro 2020]]
**[[England national football team|England]] defeats [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]] 2–1 after [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] to reach the [[UEFA Euro 2020 Final]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51198755 (BBC Sport)]
*[[2021 Stanley Cup Finals]]
**The [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] wins the Stanley Cup Finals four games to one against the [[Montreal Canadiens]]. It is their second consecutive [[Stanley Cup]] victory and their third overall. [[Andrei Vasilevskiy]] won the [[Conn Smythe Trophy]] as the MVP during the [[2021 Stanley Cup playoffs|playoffs]]. [https://www.nhl.com/news/montreal-canadiens-tampa-bay-lightning-game-5-recap/c-325483294 (NHL)]
